paper.title: Interactively Learning Preference Constraints in Linear Bandits

unmapped: Reward parameter theta is known; only the linear constraint parameter phi is unknown and observed with noise
Goal: identify argmax_{x in X, phi^T x <= tau} theta^T x (best feasible arm) with probability >= 1-delta; constraint violations allowed during exploration
Learner knows the action set X and the reward parameter theta
settings.definition_quote: A constrained linear best-arm identification (CBAI) problem $\Problem = (\ActSet, \RewParam, \ConstParam, \tau)$ consists of a finite action set $\ActSet\subset\R^d$, a reward parameter $\RewParam \in \R^d$, a constraint parameter $\ConstParam \in \R^d$, and threshold $\tau \in \R$. The decision-maker knows $\ActSet$ and $\RewParam$, but not $\ConstParam$ and $\tau$. In each iteration, the decision-maker selects an arm $\Act\in\ActSet$ and observes $\ConstParam^T \Act + \noise_\Act$, where $\noise_\Act$ is sub-Gaussian noise.

settings.name_in_paper: CBAI with oracle knowledge of the constraint parameter (oracle allocation)
unmapped: Reward parameter theta is known; constraint parameter phi observed with noise

The learner (oracle) knows the true constraint parameter phi to choose its allocation
settings.definition_quote: The oracle solution allocates samples according to $\Design^* \in \argmin_{\Design} \max_{\Act\in\BetterActSet(\BestAct)} \| \Act \|_{\DesMat^{-1}} / | \TrueConst^T \Act |$ ... this oracle solution requires knowledge of $\TrueConst$

symbols.H_lambda: max over arms x with reward >= reward of the optimal arm of ||x||^2_{A_lambda^{-1}}/(phi^T x)^2, for the allocation lambda followed by the algorithm

conditions: any allocation strategy that can distinguish between nu and nu' with probability at least 1-delta (delta-PAC)
the allocation strategy follows a probability distribution lambda over arms

source.label: thm:lower_bound
source.quote: Assume $\noise_\Act \sim \NormalDist(0, 1)$ for all $\Act\in\ActSet$. For any CBAI problem $\Problem$, there exists another CBAI problem $\Problem'$ with the same set of actions and reward parameter but a different constraint parameter and optimal arm, such that the expected number of iterations $\StoppingTime$ needed by any allocation strategy that can distinguish between $\Problem$ and $\Problem'$ with probability at least $1-\delta$ is lower bounded as ...

results.notes: Bound depends on the allocation lambda; minimizing over lambda gives H_CLB (Definition 2). Proposition (thm:instance_independent_lower_bound) shows H_CLB <= d/(C^+_min)^2, tight for some instance.

symbols.C_min: min_x |phi^T x|, smallest distance of an arm to the constraint boundary

conditions: sub-Gaussian noise (static confidence intervals with beta = sqrt(2 log(|X|/delta)), unit variance proxy implicitly)
tuning: round length N_t = max{ceil(2^{2t+3} log(|X|/delta_t)(1+eps) rho*_t), r(eps)}

source.label: thm:adaptive_algorithm_complexity
source.quote: Assume Algorithm 1 is implemented with an $\varepsilon$-approximate rounding strategy. Then, after $N$ iterations the algorithm returns an optimal arm with probability at least $1-\delta$, and we have: N \leq 8 \log(|X|\bar{t}^2/\delta^2)(1+\varepsilon) \sum_{t=1}^{\bar t} \min_\lambda \max_{x\in U_t} ... + \bar t \leq 8 \log(...) (1+\varepsilon) \bar{t} \bar{H}_{CLB}(\nu) + \bar t ... Moreover, $\WeakComplexity(\Problem) \leq d/(\MinConst)^2$

results.notes: K = |X|. eps_alg is the rounding approximation epsilon. The finer bound with sum over rounds of min-max over uncertain sets U_t is not separately recorded (data-dependent).
Obtained by combining the theorem's bound with its final statement H_bar <= d/C_min^2 (both stated in the theorem). Still depends on C_min, an instance quantity.

symbols.H_CLB: min_lambda max_{x: theta^T x >= theta^T x*} ||x||^2_{A_lambda^{-1}}/(phi^T x)^2 (Definition 2)

conditions: learner knows the constraint parameter phi
tuning: round length ceil(v^t log(|X|/delta_t)), v in (1,2)

source.label: thm:oracle_sample_complexity
source.quote: The oracle algorithm finds the optimal solution to a constrained linear best-arm identification problem $\Problem = (\ActSet, \RewParam, \ConstParam)$ within $N \propto \Complexity(\Problem)$ with probability at least $1-\delta$.

results.notes: Statement 'N ∝ H_CLB' is informal; proof says up to logarithmic factors, so recorded as O_tilde. Oracle uses true phi, not implementable.

tuning: round length ceil(v^t log(|X|/delta_t)), v in (1,2)

source.label: thm:g_allocation_sample_complexity
source.quote: G-Allocation finds the optimal arm within $N \propto d/\MinConst^2$ iterations with probability at least $1-\delta$.

results.notes: '∝' informal; proof gives t_bar(1 + 8(1+eps) log(|X|/delta_t) d/C_min^2), i.e. up to log factors.
